text:
Anya: Heads-up — we started seeing odd latency tails in canary after flipping continuous-batching v2 (CB2) yesterday night. Not massive but 95p increased ~120ms for some tenants.
Samir: Saw that too. Metrics point to increased queueing for short requests (<=8 tokens). could be batch_window_ms default change.
Maria: CB2 changed aggregation heuristics — it prefers slightly larger windows to boost throughput. That explains the tail. But why only some tenants?
Joel: Private deployments running older adapter-agent (v1.12) don't translate the new batching knob; they fall back to legacy, but routing sometimes hits hosted runtime with CB2 enabled — mismatch.
Anya: Exactly. The control-plane translates config to adapter manifests. For private/dedicated we have a translation layer that maps 'batching_strategy: cb2' -> agent flags. v1.12 lacks cb2 flags so we currently drop the field. That creates asymmetric behavior depending on runtime selected.
Samir: So some requests end up routed to CB2 backends (hosted) and see slightly higher latency for tiny requests, others remain on legacy — which gives skew in user observed latencies.
Maria: Options: 1) Make control-plane translate cb2 -> explicit legacy config for older adapters (best-effort parity). 2) Gate CB2 rollout to only runtimes that advertise cb2 capability. 3) Add runtime-side fallback: if cb2 not supported, runtime acts like cb2 but with batch_window_ms tuned down.
Joel: (3) is risky — implementing CB2 semantics in legacy runtime risks correctness/kv-cache mismatch. 1) is safer: explicitly set batch_window_ms and max_batch_size to legacy defaults when adapter doesn't advertise cb2.
infra-bot: Deploy scheduled: canary rollout paused (cb2) — see https://deploys/redwood/CB2/stop.
Anya: We should also avoid silent dropping of config fields. Control-plane should include a translation audit log when it elides or maps features.
Samir: Agreed. Action plan proposal: A) Add capability negotiation in handshake: runtime reports supported_features: ["cb2","kvcache-scoped-evict",...] B) Control-plane refuses to enable CB2 for environments that don't advertise it; it will either 1) force legacy mapping or 2) route requests to compatible pool. C) Emit audit event for mismatches.
Maria: Also add a canary flag: enable_cb2: "opt-in-by-tenant" so customers can opt into throughput-first behavior. We should not surprise enterprise tenants with latency changes.
Joel: For Dedicated we can expose a per-pool feature label — e.g., pool_features: {"cb2":"beta"}. Router will prefer pools with matching features.
Anya: Good. We should add an automated test in the manifests pipeline that validates translation idempotency: control-plane config -> adapter manifest -> round-trip decode -> equals expected runtime flags.
Samir: Small snippet for translation rule suggestion: 
```
if !adapter.supports("cb2"):
  translate("batching_strategy=cb2") -> {"batch_window_ms":8, "max_batch_size":4}
else:
  propagate("cb2")
```
Maria: Also check KV cache invariants. CB2's prefetching changed kv cache warm-up timing. If we map to smaller window, warm-up may never happen and quality could dip. Need perf regression tests with eval prompt sets.
SRE-Oncall: From incidents POV, add alert: sudden divergence between tenant percentile latencies and pool-level latencies. That'll detect translation-induced divergence early.
Anya: Ok owners: Samir will draft the translation audit events and the handshake capability field. Joel will add pool_features routing to router. Maria will add perf/regression tests for kv-cache warmup under mapped settings. I'll coordinate the canary pause/unpause and update runbook.
Samir: Drafted PR for capability field — will post link in #eng-runtime when ready.
Joel: Router change looks manageable; might need one-week lead.
infra-bot: Canary pause recorded by infra-bot at 1766543000.
Maria: Quick question: do we expose the audit events to customers (enterprise telemetry) or keep them internal? My vote: internal first, then opt-in telemetry export for Enterprise.
Anya: Internal first. We can add a usage dashboard showing feature translation counts and mismatches for enterprise customers later.
Samir: Also recommend a short-lived feature-flag 'cb2_strict_mode' that prevents fallback mapping — useful for debugging regressions.
Joel: Agreed. Will add router and control-plane checks for strict_mode so if a tenant picks strict_mode they must have compatible pool_features.
Anya: Thanks all. I'll update the rollout checklist: pause canary, add negotiation & audit, add mapping rules with explicit defaults, add perf tests, resume canary when metrics stable. ETA for negotiation+audit PR: EOD +2.
Samir: I'll post the PR link in ~3h.
Maria: I'll start perf harness runs against v1.12 with mapped defaults.
SRE-Oncall: I'll add the divergence alert and a short doc on escalation steps.
Anya: Closing loop — ping me once PRs merge, then we'll coordinate canary resume. :thumbsup:
